sets.relationshipLabel: worker and the tool of their trade
sets.explanation: Each worker is defined by the instrument they wield: the apothecary grinds with a pestle, the herbalist cuts with a sickle.

sets.relationshipLabel: drug category and a substance within it
sets.explanation: Each pair names a class of medicine followed by a classic example that belongs to it: opium is a narcotic, senna is a purgative.

sets.relationshipLabel: same liquid measure, smaller then larger
sets.explanation: Each pair climbs the same liquid-measure scale from small to large: a drop builds to a dose, a splash to a draught.

sets.relationshipLabel: traditional gathering time and the plant picked then
sets.explanation: Old herb-lore ties certain plants to a fixed moment for harvesting: St John's wort at midsummer, mandrake under a full moon.

glossary.definition: A forked, human-shaped root once believed to hold magical powers.

definitions.definition: Someone who mixes and sells medicines, like an old-time pharmacist.
A club-shaped tool for grinding things up in a bowl.
Someone who works with plants to make remedies and treatments.
A curved blade for cutting stalks and plants close to the ground.
A substance that dulls pain and makes you drowsy or sleepy.
A thick juice from poppies, used to ease pain or bring sleep.
Something that clears out your gut, used to treat constipation.
A plant whose leaves and pods are used to get things moving in your gut.
A tiny bit of liquid, the smallest amount you'd measure out.
The right amount of medicine to take at one time.
A small, quick pour of liquid, more than a drop but still modest.
A full drink or portion of liquid, swallowed in one big gulp.
The longest day of the year, right in the heart of summer.
A yellow-flowered plant used to lift the mood and heal wounds.
The night when the moon looks completely round and bright.
A forked, human-shaped root once believed to hold magical powers.
